questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's position in the world economy, as cited in January 2026:
1. India became the world's fourth-largest economy by nominal GDP in 2025, with USD 4.18 trillion, overtaking Japan.
2. In purchasing power parity terms, India is the third largest economy.
3. India's per-capita GDP in 2024 was higher than Japan's.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Government figures put India's 2025 nominal GDP at USD 4.18 trillion, ahead of Japan, and India is third in PPP terms. Per-capita income is nowhere near Japan's: USD 2,694 for India against USD 32,487 for Japan in 2024, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
The First Advance Estimates of GDP for 2025-26 were released by the National Statistics Office on 7 January 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. Real GDP growth for 2025-26 was projected at 6.5 per cent against 7.4 per cent in 2024-25.
2. Real GVA growth was projected at 7.3 per cent.
3. The GDP base year is being revised from 2011-12 to 2022-23.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The estimate is 7.4 per cent real GDP growth for 2025-26 against 6.5 per cent in 2024-25, so statement 1 reverses the two years. Real GVA growth is 7.3 per cent and nominal GDP growth 8.0 per cent. The new series on base year 2022-23 is due in February 2027.

questions.q: The Economic Survey 2025-26 projected India's real GDP growth for FY2026-27 in the range of
questions.e: The Survey, prepared by the Economic Division of the Department of Economic Affairs under the Chief Economic Adviser, estimated 7.4 per cent real GDP growth for FY2025-26 (the First Advance Estimate) and projected 6.8 to 7.2 per cent for FY2026-27. The 7.4 per cent number belongs to the current year, not the projection.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Economic Survey 2025-26:
1. Average CPI inflation for April-December 2025 was 1.7 per cent, the lowest on record.
2. Private final consumption stood at 61.5 per cent of GDP in 2025-26, the highest since 2011-12.
3. Retail inflation in 2024-25 was 1.7 per cent.
4. India's forex reserves of about USD 701.4 billion equalled roughly 11 months of import cover.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Survey records record-low inflation of 1.7 per cent for April-December 2025, private consumption at 61.5 per cent of GDP and reserves of about USD 701.4 billion (nearly 11 months of imports). Retail inflation in 2024-25 was 4.6 per cent, so statement 3 is the odd one out and three statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the CAG's Publication on State Finances 2023-24 (second edition):
1. It gives a consolidated audited picture of the finances of all 28 States.
2. States' own tax revenue is the largest component of revenue receipts, at about 47 per cent over 2014-15 to 2023-24.
3. In 2023-24 no State exceeded the 3 per cent of GSDP fiscal deficit limit recommended by the Fifteenth Finance Commission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The publication covers all 28 States with ten-year trends, and own tax revenue is the biggest revenue source. Eighteen States breached the 3 per cent fiscal deficit limit in 2023-24, so statement 3 is wrong. Sixteen States had a revenue surplus and 12 a deficit, and the share in Union taxes rose from 21.34 to 29.77 per cent.

questions.q:
India's Consumer Price Index was rebased in 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The new series has 2024 as its base year in place of 2012.
2. Its weights are drawn from the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey 2023-24.
3. It is compiled and released by the Reserve Bank of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: MoSPI, not the RBI, compiles the CPI. The new series (base 2024) uses HCES 2023-24 weights, a 358-item basket, COICOP 2018 classification, tablet-based CAPI collection and, for the first time, a rural housing index. Inflation for January 2026 on the new base was 2.75 per cent, and the food and beverages weight fell from 45.86 to 36.75 per cent.

questions.q:
The Periodic Labour Force Survey for December 2025 reported the following. Consider the statements:
1. The labour force participation rate (age 15 and above) was 56.1 per cent.
2. Rural unemployment was higher than urban unemployment.
3. Urban female unemployment was 9.1 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The survey put the all-India unemployment rate at 4.8 per cent, the labour force participation rate at 56.1 per cent and the worker population ratio at 53.4 per cent. Urban unemployment (6.7 per cent) was well above rural (3.9 per cent), and urban women were worst off at 9.1 per cent, so statement 2 is wrong.

questions.q:
Statement-I: In January 2026, the Supreme Court held that Tiger Global's 2018 sale of its Flipkart stake to Walmart is taxable in India.
Statement-II: A Tax Residency Certificate alone does not guarantee India-Mauritius treaty benefits where the real 'head and brain' of the entities lies outside Mauritius.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The Court denied the India-Mauritius DTAA benefit because the entities were controlled from outside Mauritius, so a Tax Residency Certificate was not enough. That reasoning is what makes the gains taxable, so Statement-II explains Statement-I. The ruling set aside the Delhi High Court's 2024 judgment and restored the 2020 Authority for Advance Rulings order.
questions.h: Certificate on paper, head and brain elsewhere

questions.q: Under the Reserve Bank Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2026, which comes into force on 1 July 2026, the maximum compensation for consequential financial loss is
questions.e: The scheme replaces the 2021 scheme and allows up to Rs 30 lakh for consequential financial loss and up to Rs 3 lakh for non-financial loss (such as harassment). Customers must first approach the regulated entity and may go to the Ombudsman after 30 days without response; appeals lie to an RBI Executive Director within 30 days.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs):
1. The RBI proposed in January 2026 to resume licensing of new UCBs after nearly two decades.
2. The RBI regulates UCBs' banking functions under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, while State Governments or the Central Registrar handle registration and management.
3. The first urban credit society, Anyonya Sahakari Mandali, was founded in Madras in 1904.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: UCBs are under dual control: the RBI for banking functions (licensing under Sections 22 and 23 of the BR Act) and the Registrar for management. The first urban credit society, Anyonya Sahakari Mandali, was founded in Baroda in 1889, not Madras in 1904, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) set up two expert bodies in January 2026. Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
A. Committee headed by M.S. Sahoo
B. Strategic Asset Allocation and Risk Governance (SAARG) Committee chaired by Narayan Ramachandran
List-II
1. Reviews and modernises the investment framework under the National Pension System
2. Designs a framework for assured payouts under the National Pension System
Which one of the following is the correct match?
questions.e: The 15-member Sahoo committee, headed by the former IBBI chairperson, is to design a framework for assured payouts, covering lock-in, pricing, risk and capital norms, and tax treatment. The nine-member SAARG committee has nine months to review asset allocation, alternative-investment valuation, governance and intermediary architecture for NPS investments.
questions.s: Drishti IAS, 16 Jan 2026; Vajiram & Ravi, 27 Jan 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the NPS Vatsalya Scheme Guidelines 2025 issued by PFRDA:
1. The minimum contribution is Rs 250 per year, with no maximum limit.
2. Partial withdrawal of up to 25 per cent of the minor's own contributions is allowed after three years for specified purposes such as education.
3. Non-Resident Indians and Overseas Citizens of India below 18 years are not eligible.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: NPS Vatsalya is a contributory pension scheme for minors with an account in the child's name, operated by a guardian. Contributions start at Rs 250 a year with no ceiling, and partial withdrawal of 25 per cent of own contributions is allowed after three years for education, medical treatment or specified disabilities. NRIs and OCIs below 18 are eligible, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS):
1. It was introduced on 4 February 2004 under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
2. It permits resident individuals to remit up to USD 250,000 per financial year.
3. Outward remittances under the scheme fell to a two-year low of USD 1.94 billion in November 2025, driven by lower spending on foreign education.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: LRS operates under the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999, not the Banking Regulation Act, so statement 1 is wrong. Resident individuals can remit up to USD 250,000 per financial year, and Tax Collected at Source applies to remittances above Rs 7 lakh. The November 2025 figure was a two-year low on weaker foreign-education spending.

questions.q:
Under the RBI (Priority Sector Lending - Targets and Classification) Directions, 2025, consider the following statements:
1. The PSL target for Small Finance Banks was lowered from 75 to 60 per cent of Adjusted Net Bank Credit.
2. Bank loans to the National Cooperative Development Corporation for on-lending to cooperatives now count as priority sector lending.
3. Regional Rural Banks have a PSL target of 40 per cent of Adjusted Net Bank Credit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The revised Directions cut the Small Finance Bank target to 60 per cent and recognise bank lending to NCDC as PSL, with external audit certification to avoid double counting. Domestic commercial banks must lend 40 per cent of ANBC (or CEOBE if higher) to priority sectors, while Regional Rural Banks have 75 per cent, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about FDI inflows reported by the DPIIT for April-September 2025:
1. FDI inflows were USD 35.2 billion, up 18 per cent from a year earlier.
2. Cumulative FDI since April 2000 stood at USD 1.12 trillion.
3. Mauritius was the top source of inflows.
4. Maharashtra received about 30 per cent of the inflows.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: FDI reached USD 35.2 billion in H1 FY26 (against USD 29.8 billion a year earlier), cumulative inflows since April 2000 are USD 1.12 trillion, and Maharashtra took about 30 per cent, followed by Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. Singapore (about USD 12 billion), not Mauritius, was the top source, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
NITI Aayog released the Export Preparedness Index (EPI) 2024 on 14 January 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. Karnataka was among the top five Large States.
2. The Index has four pillars, 13 sub-pillars and 70 indicators.
3. Business Ecosystem carries the highest weight, 40 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The top Large States were Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh, so Karnataka is not in the list. The Index has four pillars: Business Ecosystem (40 per cent) and Export Infrastructure, Policy and Governance, and Export Performance (20 per cent each).

questions.q:
On National Startup Day (16 January 2026) India completed ten years of Startup India. Consider the following statements on the startup definition:
1. An entity qualifies as a startup for up to 10 years from incorporation, and up to 20 years if it is a deep tech startup.
2. Its turnover must not have exceeded Rs 200 crore in any year since incorporation, or Rs 300 crore for a deep tech startup.
3. Public limited companies are among the eligible legal forms.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Startups can be a private limited company, partnership firm, LLP or cooperative society, not a public limited company. The age and turnover limits are 10 years and Rs 200 crore, rising to 20 years and Rs 300 crore for deep tech. The Fund of Funds (Rs 10,000 crore, run by SIDBI) and the Seed Fund Scheme (Rs 945 crore) are the main funding supports.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the NITI Aayog report 'Achieving Efficiencies in MSME Sector through Convergence of Schemes':
1. It was prepared by the Ministry of MSME.
2. It proposes merging SFURTI with the MSE-CDP.
3. The Udyam portal has 3.94 crore registered MSMEs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The report is by NITI Aayog, not the Ministry of MSME. It proposes converging more than 18 MSME schemes through information convergence and process convergence, including merging SFURTI with MSE-CDP. The Udyam portal has 3.94 crore registered MSMEs, and MSMEs contribute 27 to 30 per cent of GDP.

questions.q: The Union Cabinet in January 2026 approved Rs 5,000 crore of equity infusion into SIDBI over three years. SIDBI was set up under, and is headquartered at,
questions.e: SIDBI is the apex financing institution for MSMEs, created under the Small Industries Development Bank of India Act, 1989, and headquartered in Lucknow. The extra capital is meant to expand MSME credit, with beneficiaries projected to rise from 76.26 lakh in FY25 to about 102 lakh by FY28.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Design Linked Incentive (DLI) scheme under the Semicon India Programme:
1. It is implemented by MeitY.
2. It offers up to 50 per cent of eligible design expenditure, capped at Rs 30 crore per application.
3. C-DAC is the nodal agency of the Semicon India Programme.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The DLI scheme gives up to 50 per cent of eligible design expenditure capped at Rs 15 crore per application, plus 4 to 6 per cent of net sales for five years capped at Rs 30 crore, so the caps in statement 2 are swapped. MeitY implements it, C-DAC is the nodal agency of the Rs 76,000 crore Semicon India Programme, and 24 chip-design projects have been sanctioned.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for White Goods:
1. It covers refrigerators and washing machines.
2. It offers 4 to 6 per cent incentive on incremental sales for five years.
3. The base year for incremental turnover is 2019-20.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Five companies were selected in January 2026 under the scheme, which covers air conditioners and LED lights, not refrigerators and washing machines. The incentive is 4 to 6 per cent on incremental sales for five years, with 2019-20 as the base year; the scheme runs from FY2021-22 to FY2028-29 and DPIIT is the nodal body.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Tex-RAMPS, for which the Ministry of Textiles signed MoUs with 15 States at Guwahati in January 2026:
1. It is a fully centrally funded scheme.
2. It runs from FY2025-26 to FY2030-31.
3. Each State or UT gets Rs 1 lakh per year and each district Rs 12 lakh per year.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Tex-RAMPS is fully centrally funded and runs from FY2025-26 to FY2030-31, supporting a goal of a USD 350 billion textile industry. The sums are reversed in statement 3: each State or UT gets Rs 12 lakh a year and each district Rs 1 lakh a year, so two statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about rice in India, as reported in January 2026:
1. India's rice production of 150.18 million tonnes exceeded China's 145.28 million tonnes.
2. India supplies about 40 per cent of global rice exports.
3. Rice is primarily a rabi crop in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Agriculture Minister said India is now the world's largest rice producer, with about 40 per cent of global rice exports above 20 million tonnes. Rice is primarily a Kharif crop needing about 150 cm of rainfall and 25 to 35 degrees Celsius, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about milk production in India:
1. Uttar Pradesh was the largest producer in 2024-25, with a 15.66 per cent share.
2. White Revolution 2.0 was launched by the Ministry of Agriculture on 19 September 2024.
3. Operation Flood was launched by the National Dairy Development Board in 1980.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India's milk output was 247.87 million tonnes in 2024-25, up 3.58 per cent, with Uttar Pradesh the leading producer. White Revolution 2.0 was launched by the Ministry of Cooperation, and Operation Flood was launched on 13 January 1970 by NDDB under Verghese Kurien. Only statement 1 is correct.

questions.q:
Coking coal was included in January 2026 in Part D of the First Schedule of the MMDR Act, 1957. Consider the following statements:
1. Part D lists critical and strategic minerals.
2. About 95 per cent of the steel sector's coking coal requirement is met through imports.
3. India's coking coal reserves lie mainly in Rajasthan and Gujarat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Listing coking coal as a critical and strategic mineral is meant to speed up approvals, exploration and deep-seated mining for the steel industry, which imports about 95 per cent of its needs. Reserves of about 37.37 billion tonnes lie mainly in Jharkhand, with others in Madhya Pradesh, West Bengal and Chhattisgarh, so statement 3 is wrong.
